function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning: The user says: "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" They want to calculate the standard deviation for a null hypothesis test? Actually they give sample mean 98.2, sample std dev 1.4, sample size 40, and want to get population mean 98.6. They might want to compute the p-value? Or compute the standard error? The phrase "零假設檢定的標準差" maybe means "standard deviation for the null hypothesis test"? Might be they want to compute the standard error of the mean difference? Or compute the t-statistic? Let's interpret: They have sample mean 98.2, sample std dev 1.4, n=40. Null hypothesis: population mean = 98.6. They want to compute the standard deviation of the sampling distribution under null? That would be sigma/sqrt(n). But we don't know population sigma; we use sample std dev as estimate. So standard error = 1.4 / sqrt(40) ≈ 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2215. Then t-statistic = (98.2 - 98.6) / 0.2215 ≈ -0.4 / 0.2215 ≈ -1.805. Then p-value two-tailed: 2 * P(T > |t|) with df=39. We can compute approximate p-value using t distribution. Let's approximate: t=1.805, df=39. Using t table: For df=40, t=1.684 gives p=0.10, t=2.021 gives p=0.05. So t=1.805 gives p between 0.10 and 0.05, maybe ~0.08. So p-value ~0.08.
